name: Persian-to-Braille
summary: Translate selected Persian text to Unicode Braille in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
description:
Translate selected Persian text to Braille through the shared Persian-to-Braille SDK.

Persian-to-Braille helps people who work with Persian text create Unicode Braille directly inside Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. The add-in is designed for accessibility-focused workflows where a user needs a clear, repeatable way to convert selected Persian content without copying the document into a separate translation service.

In Word, select Persian text and open the Persian-to-Braille task pane to preview the translation. A successful result can replace the current selection or be inserted after it. In Excel, select one plain-text cell to preview and replace its contents with the translated Braille result. In PowerPoint, select a text range and replace it after reviewing the preview. Each host uses selection checks before writing back so that a stale preview is not silently applied to changed content.

The Microsoft 365 integration uses the same public Persian-to-Braille SDK as the standalone project. The Office layer does not implement a separate translation table. This keeps Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CLI, web, and future integrations aligned with the same core translation behavior.

The current release is intended for users, educators, accessibility specialists, developers, and organizations working with Persian-language Braille content. It can support document preparation, educational material, accessibility testing, demonstrations, and workflows that need Unicode Braille output for selected Persian text.

No publisher-controlled account, sign-in flow, analytics system, or cloud translation service is required by the audited add-in release. Translation runs through the client-side SDK and Core. Microsoft Office infrastructure, Office.js, the user’s Microsoft 365 environment, and the project’s static hosting remain separate platform services governed by their own terms and technical processing.

Persian-to-Braille is an open-source project. The Core and SDK are released under the MIT License. Support, privacy information, and end-user terms are available from the project’s public HTTPS pages for users and organizations worldwide.
